Method: Derived from the GNU ld map in evidence/output.map.gz, parsed by cres_t4.service.linker_map.parse -- which reads a RISC-V map with no changes -- and cross-checked against `riscv64-unknown-elf-ar t`. Versions and licences carry over from the recorded commit: the same tree as cases 002 and 003.
Matching: A candidate component matches when its name, lower-cased with punctuation removed, equals the entry's Name or any of its AcceptableNames.

Components.Name: Mbed TLS
Components.VersionNote: MBEDTLS_VERSION_STRING in the built tree at 107ea89d, tag v3.6.2.
Components.LicenceNote: LICENSE in the built tree plus the SPDX-License-Identifier of aes.c, sha256.c and platform_util.c -- the three sources whose members are in this image.
Components.Uncertainty: THE SAME THREE MEMBERS AS CASES 002 AND 003, which is the point of this case existing. The archive is 156KB here against 94KB on Cortex-M -- RISC-V encodes the same source larger -- and the image needs the same three translation units. 'Which members ship' is a property of the program, not of the linker and not of the architecture.

Components.Name: libgcc
Components.VersionNote: From the archive's own path (/usr/lib/gcc/riscv64-unknown-elf/12.2.0/rv64imac/lp64/), which is the compiler's version. Heuristic because a filesystem layout is not a manifest.
Components.LicenceNote: libgcc's published terms. The runtime exception is the half that matters to a device maker and the half most tools drop.
Components.Uncertainty: AN ARCHITECTURE-SPECIFIC DEPENDENCY THAT APPEARS IN NO SOURCE FILE. Base RISC-V has no byte-swap instruction, so mbed TLS's SHA-256 calls libgcc's __bswapsi2 where ARM got a single `rev`. The link fails outright without -lgcc. libgcc is a component of THIS image and of case 002's (division helpers) and of NEITHER case 003's -- so even the compiler runtime's presence is a property of the architecture and the configuration, not of the project. Exactly what a source-tree scanner cannot find.

NotComponents.Name: the application
NotComponents.Why: First-party code -- app.c, including the memcpy and memset the freestanding build needs. One object, 334 bytes.

Open.Question: Does the total reconcile?
Open.Detail: 18216 + 1298 = 19514 across the two components, plus 334 of first-party code = 19848, which is the map's own LinkedBytes. It reconciles exactly.

Open.Question: Why is there no picolibc component?
Open.Detail: The link is -nostdlib, so picolibc supplies headers at compile time and nothing at link time -- app.c provides its own memcpy and memset. picolibc is a BUILD dependency and not a component of the image, and the distinction is one a tool reading the build rather than the link would get wrong.

RevisionNote: CORRECTED 2026-10-13: re-established after both map readers were fixed to stop counting output sections that are in the ELF file but not in the device (.debug_*, .comment, .ARM.attributes, .riscv.attributes). The previous figure is kept as PreviousLinkedBytes.
